usage: This is the standard and universally understood greeting for good morning in Modern Standard Arabic, used until around noon. It is appropriate for all formalities, from news broadcasts to casual conversations, and does not change based on the gender or number of people being addressed.

variants.label: formal to a group
variants.english: May God make your morning happy
variants.note: A highly formal greeting often used by news anchors or public speakers addressing an audience.

variants.label: formal to a man
variants.english: May God make your morning happy
variants.note: Used in formal correspondence or very polite conversation when addressing a single male.

variants.label: formal to a woman
variants.english: May God make your morning happy
variants.note: Used in formal correspondence or very polite conversation when addressing a single female.

examples.arabic: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْرِ يَا سَيِّدِي، كَيْفَ حَالُكَ الْيَوْمَ؟
examples.transliteration: saba7u al-khayr ya sayyidi, kayfa 7aluka al-yawm?
examples.english: Good morning sir, how are you today?
Good morning to all the listeners.

examples.arabic: قَالَتْ لَهُ صَبَاحُ الْخَيْرِ قَبْلَ أَنْ تَذْهَبَ إِلَى الْعَمَلِ.
examples.transliteration: qalat lahu saba7u al-khayr qabla an tathhaba ila al-3amal.
examples.english: She said good morning to him before going to work.
